title: Surrealist founders' occult séances and Breton's 1922 article

tellings.quote: these guys from the beginning of even from before it took the name surrealism were constantly engaged in occult rituals including long seances

plain: The claim is that the founders of surrealism in 1920s France, including André Breton, Max Ernst and Paul Éluard, were from the very start, even before the movement had its name, "constantly engaged in occult rituals including long seances", and that Breton wrote about this in a 1922 article. A researcher named Jason Jorjani says this to Michels, without naming a source, to suggest that a famous art movement grew out of occult practice.
